messages.author: 521ff3d3469cb28a
messages.subject: Covariates
parts:
Dear Methylkit,
I've completed my analysis, but when I look at a qq plot of the p-values (or q-values) there appears to be an excess of low p-values. In the output file, there are a number of sites where both the p-value and the q-value are zero. I'm wondering if this is normal, and if there is a way to control for covariates such as age, gender, etc that are known to influence methylation? If the analysis is a linear model, presumably there is a way to do this?
Thanks,
Juan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Covariates
parts:
Hi Juan, There is some code under development to add covariates. You can also look at batch effect functions we have that use PCA to remove the effect of covariates (not the best way). You can talk to Dhruva from Mason lab if you are still at ICB, he may have working code for covariates.

Best
Altuna
